title: SLO credit bands and graceful degradation matrix for model capacity tiers
creator: Anika Patel
description: Create a formal SLO crediting and degradation policy that maps model capacity tiers to SLO credit bands, defines graded degradation bands, and specifies operational circuit-breaker thresholds for multi-region failover and load-shedding. This will standardize how endpoints borrow/repay error budget and how the control plane triggers soft vs hard evictions across Dedicated/Hosted/Private deployments.
background: We currently have a mix of ad-hoc SLO treatments for model endpoints: some routes are allowed to degrade to cheap quantized variants, others are evicted entirely. This inconsistency causes customer confusion, unpredictable error budget consumption, and opaque operational playbooks when capacity constraints surface across regions.
goals: 1) Define a deterministic SLO credit-band model tied to model capacity tier and route class. 2) Specify a three-band graceful degradation matrix (Green/Amber/Red) with concrete artifact actions (cache reuse, quantized variant fallback, soft-eviction). 3) Define circuit-breaker thresholds and recovery behavior for multi-region failover. 4) Produce a migration plan and runbook for rollout with observability hooks.
scope: Includes all LLM inference routes exposed by the Redwood API and Dedicated pools. Excludes internal admin-only endpoints and experimental beta variants. Applies to text generation, chat, and embedding routes; does not change pricing.
deliverables: 1) Policy document summarizing credit bands and degradation actions. 2) A JSON manifest format for per-endpoint SLO metadata (to be consumed by routing layer). 3) Dashboard panels and alerts for tracking band transitions and credit transfers. 4) Runbook for on-call and SEs describing mitigation actions and rollback steps.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Policy reviewed and approved by Reliability, Product, and Solutions Eng. 2) Routing layer accepts SLO manifest schema and can query band for an endpoint. 3) Demo of multi-region failover with soft-eviction exercised in staging. 4) Observability shows correct band transitions and error-budget accounting in staging for a synthetic workload.
proposed_policy:
- Model capacity tiers: NANO, MICRO, STANDARD, TURBO. Each tier has an associated SLO credit allocation per 24h window (NANO: 2000 credits, MICRO: 10k, STANDARD: 50k, TURBO: 250k). Credits map to token-equivalent units.
- Graded degradation bands: GREEN (>=80% credits remaining) => normal routing; AMBER (50-80%) => enable prefix caching and recommend quantized variants for non-pinned routes; RED (<50%) => apply soft-eviction to lowest-priority variants and degrade to pre-approved fallback models, enable regional diversion.
- Circuit breakers: soft-breaker at 30% of per-cluster capacity for sustained 2m => trigger AMBER policies; hard-breaker at 60% sustained 30s over capacity => immediate RED actions and region-level failover.
- Borrow/Lend semantics: endpoints can borrow up to 10% from pinned sibling variants within the same tenant pool; borrowed credits must be repaid within 48h or are reclaimed by the tenancy arbiter.
- Priority matrix: customer routes marked 'SLO-critical' may be exempt from automatic hard-eviction but still subject to throttling and token-price-based shedding.
telemetry_and_alerting:
- New metrics: endpoint.slo_credits_remaining, endpoint.degradation_band, endpoint.borrowed_credit, endpoint.soft_eviction_count.
- Alerts: P0 alarm when any global model tier moves to RED across >2 zones; P1 alert when a single region shows soft-eviction >5m.
- Dashboards: per-tenant and per-model time-series for credit burn-rate, borrow/lend flows, and band transition heatmaps.
manifest_schema_notes: Provide a flat JSON manifest per endpoint with: key, model_tier, base_credit_allocation, priority_label, allowed_fallbacks (list of model ids), auto_requantize_allowed (true/false as string), can_borrow (true/false as string). Implementation PR will include exact field names and versioning.
migration_steps: 1) Author a seed manifest for top 50 customers and route types in staging.
2) Run canary: enable policy read-path for 10% of traffic to measure band transitions without enforcement (shadow mode).
3) Flip enforcement for non-critical tenants in staging and validate automatic fallbacks.
4) Roll out enforcement to Dedicated pools with a 24h observation window between steps.
5) Full roll to Hosted with a weekend maintenance window and live monitoring runbook active.
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with Reliability, Serving Runtime, and Product. Agreed that credit units map to token-equivalents and must be exposed in telemetry.
2026-02-28: Draft policy posted; preliminary numbers for credit allocations discussed. UX impact noted for pinned model routes and 'friction-free' enterprise customers.
2026-03-05: Prototype manifest schema v0.1 implemented in routing service; returns band in staging for mock endpoints. PR: github.com/redwood/routing/pull/1142 (link below).
2026-03-09: Game-day simulation planned for 2026-03-18 to exercise soft/hard breakers using traffic-replay tools. Ops runbook draft created.
2026-03-12: Reliability review feedback: reduce hard-breaker sensitivity for TURBO tier by 25% to prevent oscillation. Updating thresholds.
decisions: Use credit-based accounting (token-equivalent credits) instead of simple request-count SLOs to align with variable-cost routes.
Adopt three-band (Green/Amber/Red) model rather than many granular bands to simplify operator response and UI surface area.
Implement borrow/lend within tenant pools only; cross-tenant borrowing is disallowed.
Circuit-breaker thresholds will be configurable per-region and per-tier; defaults will be provided in the manifest.
All enforcement will initially be opt-in for Dedicated customers and opt-out for Hosted customers for the first 6 weeks.
Represent booleans in manifest as strings for forward compatibility in the routing service (e.g., "true").
risks: Risk: Aggressive hard-eviction may cause customer SLA violations if fallback model quality is unacceptable.
Risk: Incorrect credit mapping leads to unfair throttling for long-context routes.
Risk: Observability gaps may make band transitions invisible until customers complain.
mitigation: Mitigation: Introduce a quality gate for fallback models — they must pass a short promptset eval before being eligible for RED fallback.
Mitigation: Provide per-route calibration tool to estimate token-equivalent credit costs for long-context endpoints.
Mitigation: Add synthetic probes and heartbeat endpoints to validate dashboard correctness before rollout.
